bank.instruction: Make this look like a comic book photo
bank.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

outcomes.description: Transform the image so it has a comic-book visual style while retaining its photographic subject matter.
outcomes.target: The image visibly combines comic-book styling with a photographic appearance.
outcomes.reference: The supplied image, as edited; assess the overall visual treatment for comic-book styling and photographic subject matter.

bank.reason: The requested appearance can be represented with separate evidence for comic-book styling, photographic appearance, and whether the edited image shows any requested styling progress relative to the source. The third fact prevents an unchanged photographic appearance from being mistaken for partial progress.

facts.question: Does the edited image visibly have comic-book-style visual treatment?
facts.present_when: The edited image has clearly visible visual treatment characteristic of comic-book imagery, such as ink-like contours, graphic color treatment, or comparable comic-book styling.
facts.absent_when: The image is clear enough to assess and shows no visible comic-book-style treatment.
facts.unknown_when: The edited image is unavailable or too unclear to assess its visual treatment.

facts.question: Does the edited image still read as a photograph of its depicted subject?
facts.present_when: The depicted subject retains a photographic appearance.
facts.absent_when: The image is clear enough to assess and no longer reads as a photograph of its subject.
facts.unknown_when: The edited image is unavailable or too unclear to assess whether it reads as a photograph.

facts.question: Compared with the source, does the edited image show any visible progress toward comic-book styling?
facts.present_when: The edited image shows a visible change toward comic-book styling, even if the requested combined appearance is not achieved.
facts.absent_when: The source and edited image are assessable, and the edited image shows no visible change toward comic-book styling.
facts.unknown_when: The source or edited image is unavailable or too unclear to determine whether there is visible progress toward comic-book styling.

decisions.complete_when: F1 is present and F2 is present.
decisions.partial_when: F3 is present, but the complete condition is not met.
decisions.unknown_when: The complete condition is not established, F3 is not present, and F3 is unknown; or F3 is present but F1 or F2 is unknown, so completion cannot be determined.

audit.reason: F1 and F2 are independently assessable, but F3 asks for comparative progress toward styling, which overlaps F1 and is not a distinct visual property. More importantly, the decision rules can label F3-present as partial even when F1 is present and F2 is absent, although the requested combined appearance may already be fully achieved only when both are present; the criteria also leave some combinations (for example, F3 absent with F1/F2 unknown) without a clear result. The bank therefore does not reliably preserve the rubric’s complete/partial/absent distinctions.

bank.instruction: Make this look like a comic book photo
bank.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

outcomes.description: Transform the image so it has a comic-book visual style while retaining its photographic subject matter.
outcomes.target: The image visibly combines comic-book styling with a photographic appearance.
outcomes.reference: The supplied image, as edited; assess the overall visual treatment for comic-book styling and photographic subject matter.

facts.question: Does the edited image show comic-book-style outlines or ink-like contouring?
facts.present_when: Distinct outlines or ink-like contouring are visibly applied to scene elements in the edited image.
facts.absent_when: Scene elements lack visible comic-book-style outlines or ink-like contouring.
facts.unknown_when: The edited image is unavailable or too unclear to assess outlines or contouring.

facts.question: Does the edited image show comic-book-style color treatment, such as flat or posterized color areas?
facts.present_when: Colors visibly appear flattened, posterized, or otherwise treated in a comic-book-like way.
facts.absent_when: Colors retain an ordinary photographic tonal treatment without visible comic-book-style flattening or posterization.
facts.unknown_when: The edited image is unavailable or too unclear to assess its color treatment.

facts.question: Does the edited image still read as a photograph of its depicted street scene?
facts.present_when: The depicted street scene retains a photographic appearance, with recognizable photographic detail and tonal variation.
facts.absent_when: The scene no longer reads as a photograph, for example because it appears wholly illustrated or graphic.
facts.unknown_when: The edited image is unavailable or too unclear to assess whether the scene reads as a photograph.

decisions.complete_when: F1 or F2 is present, and F3 is present: comic-book styling is visibly applied while the scene still reads as a photograph.
decisions.partial_when: At least one of F1 or F2 is present, but the complete condition is not met; this includes styling evidence with F3 absent, or photographic appearance with no comic-book styling evidence.
decisions.absent_when: F1 and F2 are both absent, with F3 either present or absent; there is no observed progress toward comic-book styling.
decisions.unknown_when: The observations do not establish complete, partial, or absent fulfillment because relevant facts are unknown and the known observations do not settle the outcome.

audit.reason: The facts are individually assessable, but the decision criteria weaken the requested complete/partial distinction: F1 or F2 alone can establish completion, although the saved criterion requires comic-book styling clearly applied while the image still reads as a photograph. The partial rule also labels photographic appearance with no styling evidence as partial, contradicting the rubric’s no-progress definition and the absent rule. The criteria therefore do not reliably preserve the requested semantics.
